sections.title: Form and cultivation
sections.text: A perennial about 0.6–1.5 m tall, native to eastern Europe and western Asia and now widely cultivated. It has large basal leaves and clusters of small, four-petalled white flowers. Its thick, fleshy root is harvested as a pungent condiment.

sections.title: Food
sections.text: The root is eaten as a condiment; the leaves are also edible but rarely consumed. The large pale root in the plate is the harvested plant part, not a fruit.
